
# diagnostics

```{r}

#This line reads the powerBullFunctions.R script so that those
#functions are in the global environment.
source("powerBullFunctions.R")

#Define the directory where the data files are saved.
dataDir = "../../../data/stanley et al. 2018/raw/"

#Grab the names of all fo the files in dataDire
nameF = list.files(path = dataDir)

#Initialize variables to fill in
NAME = avgES = medSE = I_sq = FE_est = RE_est = rep(NA,length(nameF)) 
WLS_est = WW_est = PP_est = FAT_sig = PET_sig = rep(NA,length(nameF))
kAdq_WL = kAdq_PP = kAdq_WW = prAdq_WL = prAdq_PP = prAdq_WW = rep(NA,length(nameF))  
pow_WL = pow_PP = pow_WW = rep(NA,length(nameF))


#Begin loop over each of the datasets
for(i in 1:length(nameF)){
  
  print(paste0("Read in and analyze dataset ",i))
  
  #Read in dataset i
  dat = read.dta13(file = paste0("../../../data/stanley et al. 2018/raw/", nameF[i]))
  
  #Define the name for dataset i
  NAME[i] = strsplit(nameF[i],".dta")[[1]]
  
  #Define variance for dataset i 
  v = dat$SE^2
  
  #Run analyses on dataset i and extract results
  avgES[i]   = mean(dat$es,na.rm=T)
  medSE[i]   = median(dat$SE,na.rm=T)
  I_sq[i]    = RMA.est (dat$es,v)$value[7]
  FE_est[i]  = as.numeric(rma(dat$es,v,method="FE")$b)
  RE_est[i]  = RMA.est (dat$es,v)$value[1]
  WLS_est[i] = WLS.est(dat$es,v)$value[1]
  WW_est[i]  = as.numeric(WAAP.est(dat$es, v)$value[1])
  PP_est[i]  = PETPEESE.est(dat$es, v)$value[25]
  FAT_sig[i] = PETPEESE.est(dat$es, v)$value[22] < 0.10
  PET_sig[i] = PETPEESE.est(dat$es, v)$value[16] < 0.10
  
  pow_WL[i] = 1 - pnorm(1.96 - abs(WLS_est[i])/medSE[i])
  pow_PP[i] = 1 - pnorm(1.96 - abs(PP_est[i])/medSE[i])
  pow_WW[i] = 1 - pnorm(1.96 - abs(WW_est[i])/medSE[i])
  
  kAdq_WL[i] = sum(dat$SE < abs(WLS_est[i])/2.8, na.rm = T)
  kAdq_PP[i] = sum(dat$SE < abs(PP_est[i])/2.8,na.rm = T)
  kAdq_WW[i] = sum(dat$SE < abs(WW_est[i])/2.8,na.rm = T)
  prAdq_WL[i] = kAdq_WL[i]/sum(!is.na(dat$SE))
  prAdq_PP[i] = kAdq_PP[i]/sum(!is.na(dat$SE))
  prAdq_WW[i] = kAdq_WW[i]/sum(!is.na(dat$SE))

}

#Compile results from the loop into a dataframe
output = data.frame(
  NAME,    
  avgES,   
  medSE, 
  I_sq,
  FE_est,  
  RE_est,  
  WLS_est, 
  WW_est,  
  PP_est,  
  FAT_sig, 
  PET_sig,
  pow_WL,
  pow_PP,
  pow_WW,
  kAdq_WL, 
  kAdq_PP, 
  kAdq_WW,
  prAdq_WL, 
  prAdq_PP, 
  prAdq_WW
) 

#get median power for each MA
print(paste0("Median of median power, based on WLS: ",round(median(output$pow_WL,na.rm=T),3)))
print(paste0("Median of median power, based on WAAP: ",round(median(output$pow_WW,na.rm=T),3)))
print(paste0("Median of median power, based on PET-PEESE: ",round(median(output$pow_PP,na.rm=T),3)))

#get median proportions of adequately powered
print(paste0("Median proportion of adequately powered, based on WLS: ",round(median(output$prAdq_WL),3)))
print(paste0("Median proportion of adequately powered, based on WAAP: ",round(median(output$prAdq_WW),3)))
print(paste0("Median proportion of adequately powered, based on PET-PEESE: ",round(median(output$prAdq_PP),3)))

print(paste0("Median I^2: ",round(median(output$I_sq),3)))

print(paste0("Median absolute value of average effect size: ",round(median(abs(output$avgES)),3)))
print(paste0("Median absolute value of WLS estimate: ",round(median(abs(output$WLS_est)),3)))
print(paste0("Median absolute value of WAAP estimate: ",round(median(abs(output$WW_est)),3)))
print(paste0("Median absolute value of PET-PEESE estimate: ",round(median(abs(output$PP_est)),3)))


#Write the dataframe as a .csv file
write.csv(output,file="../../../data/stanley et al. 2018/outputs/results_original.csv")


```


# Comparisons

## Check 1: Do all files have the same structure?

```{r}

# Additional Diagnostics: Why Might Row Counts Differ?

library(haven)
library(fs)
library(tidyverse)

files <- dir_ls("../../../data/stanley et al. 2018/raw/", glob = "*.dta")

structure_check <- map_dfr(files, function(f) {
  dat <- read_dta(f)
  cols <- names(dat)
  
  tibble(
    file = basename(f),
    n_rows = nrow(dat),
    n_cols = ncol(dat),
    has_es = "es" %in% cols,
    has_SE = "SE" %in% cols,
    n_es_nonmissing = sum(!is.na(dat$es)),
    n_SE_nonmissing = sum(!is.na(dat$SE)),
    n_both_nonmissing = sum(!is.na(dat$es) & !is.na(dat$SE)),
    all_cols = paste(cols, collapse = ", ")
  )
})

cat("=== FILES SUMMARY ===\n")
print(structure_check %>% select(file, n_rows, n_es_nonmissing, n_SE_nonmissing, n_both_nonmissing))

```

## Check 2: Compare total rows between approaches

```{r}
# Original approach: sum of rows across files
total_rows_original <- sum(structure_check$n_rows)

# Rewrite approach: read all files and stack
dat_raw_rewrite <- dir_ls("../../../data/stanley et al. 2018/raw/", glob = "*.dta") %>%
  map_dfr(~read_dta(.x) %>% mutate(across(everything(), as.character)), .id = "source_file")

total_rows_rewrite <- nrow(dat_raw_rewrite)

cat("\n=== ROW COUNT COMPARISON ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Original approach would process: %d rows (sum of individual files)\n", total_rows_original))
cat(sprintf("Rewrite approach processes: %d rows (stacked dataframe)\n", total_rows_rewrite))
cat(sprintf("Difference: %d rows\n", total_rows_rewrite - total_rows_original))

if (total_rows_original != total_rows_rewrite) {
  cat("\n⚠️  WARNING: Row counts differ! This suggests:\n")
  cat("   - Duplicate rows being added during stacking, OR\n")
  cat("   - Files being read multiple times, OR\n") 
  cat("   - Some other data processing difference\n")
}

```

## Check 3: Are there rows with missing es or SE?

```{r}
# For original: count rows that would be USED (non-missing for both)
usable_rows_original <- sum(structure_check$n_both_nonmissing)

# For rewrite: count after your coalesce logic
dat_cleaned_rewrite <- dat_raw_rewrite %>%
  mutate(
    yi = as.numeric(coalesce(
      r, correlation, d, g, es, fischer, z, averager, dreportedinpaper
    )),
    sei = case_when(
      !is.na(SE) ~ as.numeric(SE),
      !is.na(se) ~ as.numeric(se),
      !is.na(sed) ~ as.numeric(sed),
      !is.na(SEd) ~ as.numeric(SEd),
      !is.na(sefischer) ~ as.numeric(sefischer),
      !is.na(SEused) ~ as.numeric(SEused),
      !is.na(variance) ~ sqrt(as.numeric(variance)),
      !is.na(Variance) ~ sqrt(as.numeric(Variance)),
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )

usable_rows_rewrite <- sum(!is.na(dat_cleaned_rewrite$yi) & !is.na(dat_cleaned_rewrite$sei))

cat("\n=== USABLE ROWS COMPARISON ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Original: %d rows with non-missing es AND SE\n", usable_rows_original))
cat(sprintf("Rewrite: %d rows with non-missing yi AND sei\n", usable_rows_rewrite))
cat(sprintf("Difference: %d rows\n", usable_rows_rewrite - usable_rows_original))

if (usable_rows_original != usable_rows_rewrite) {
  cat("\n⚠️  DIFFERENCE FOUND!\n")
  sprintf("   The rewrite captures %d %s usable effect sizes\n", 
      abs(usable_rows_rewrite - usable_rows_original),
      ifelse(usable_rows_rewrite > usable_rows_original, "MORE", "FEWER"))
}

```

## Check 4: Are there any alternative columns with data?

```{r}

# Check if ANY of the alternative columns you're checking have data
alternative_check <- map_dfr(files, function(f) {
  dat <- read_dta(f)
  cols <- names(dat)
  
  tibble(
    file = basename(f),
    # Effect size alternatives
    has_r = "r" %in% cols,
    has_correlation = "correlation" %in% cols,
    has_d = "d" %in% cols,
    has_g = "g" %in% cols,
    has_fischer = "fischer" %in% cols,
    has_z = "z" %in% cols,
    # SE alternatives  
    has_se_lower = "se" %in% cols,
    has_sed = "sed" %in% cols,
    has_variance = "variance" %in% cols,
    # Check if they have NON-MISSING data
    r_nonmissing = if("r" %in% cols) sum(!is.na(dat$r)) else 0,
    correlation_nonmissing = if("correlation" %in% cols) sum(!is.na(dat$correlation)) else 0,
    d_nonmissing = if("d" %in% cols) sum(!is.na(dat$d)) else 0,
    g_nonmissing = if("g" %in% cols) sum(!is.na(dat$g)) else 0,
    se_lower_nonmissing = if("se" %in% cols) sum(!is.na(dat$se)) else 0,
    variance_nonmissing = if("variance" %in% cols) sum(!is.na(dat$variance)) else 0
  )
})

cat("\n=== ALTERNATIVE COLUMNS CHECK ===\n")
alternative_summary <- alternative_check %>%
  summarise(
    files_with_r = sum(r_nonmissing > 0),
    files_with_correlation = sum(correlation_nonmissing > 0),
    files_with_d = sum(d_nonmissing > 0),
    files_with_g = sum(g_nonmissing > 0),
    files_with_se_lower = sum(se_lower_nonmissing > 0),
    files_with_variance = sum(variance_nonmissing > 0),
    total_files = n()
  )

print(alternative_summary)

if (alternative_summary$files_with_r > 0 || 
    alternative_summary$files_with_correlation > 0 ||
    alternative_summary$files_with_d > 0) {
  cat("\n⚠️  Some files have data in alternative effect size columns!\n")
  cat("   Your coalesce() logic may be capturing these.\n")
}

```

## Check 5: Key Question - Does coalesce capture MORE than es alone?

```{r}

cat("\n=== COALESCE BENEFIT CHECK ===\n")

# Simulate what original gets (just es)
just_es <- dat_raw_rewrite %>%
  mutate(
    yi_original = as.numeric(es),
    sei_original = as.numeric(SE)
  )

n_original_method <- sum(!is.na(just_es$yi_original) & !is.na(just_es$sei_original))

# What rewrite gets (coalesce)
n_rewrite_method <- usable_rows_rewrite

cat(sprintf("Using ONLY es column: %d usable rows\n", n_original_method))
cat(sprintf("Using coalesce() logic: %d usable rows\n", n_rewrite_method))
cat(sprintf("Extra rows captured by coalesce: %d\n", n_rewrite_method - n_original_method))

if (n_rewrite_method > n_original_method) {
  # Find which rows are captured by coalesce but not by es
  extra_rows <- dat_cleaned_rewrite %>%
    mutate(yi_original = as.numeric(es)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(yi) & !is.na(sei)) %>%
    filter(is.na(yi_original))
  
  cat(sprintf("\n✓ Coalesce captures %d additional rows!\n", nrow(extra_rows)))
  cat("These rows have data in alternative columns:\n")
  print(head(extra_rows %>% select(source_file, yi, sei)))
} else {
  cat("\n✓ Coalesce provides NO additional benefit - all data is in 'es' column\n")
}

```
